verdict: A quiet day dominated by SEO comparison spam and routine model-card updates; only a handful of items carry real pipeline relevance.

stories.headline: Lightricks ships a wide set of LTX-2.3/2.5 IC-LoRAs for video-to-video tasks
stories.body: Lightricks published a batch of task-specific LoRAs for its LTX-2.3 and LTX-2.5 video models: deblur, water simulation, pixel upscaling, instant-shave/character-consistency, cinemagraph, slow-motion control, and foley video-to-audio. All are gated under Lightricks' custom licence, distributed as diffusion-single-file checkpoints on Hugging Face. Several have thousands of downloads, suggesting real community uptake. No VRAM figures given; base models run at 22B parameters.
stories.why: Task-specific LoRAs on an open video model are the kind of thing that gets wired into a ComfyUI restyle pipeline fast.

stories.headline: Brahma AI's Emmy-winning face replacement tech is heading into Nuke
stories.body: Brahma AI co-founder Jo Plaete discussed the company's Neural Performance tech, which shared a 2026 Technology & Engineering Emmy with Disney Research, Digital Domain and Rising Sun Pictures. The company says a $150M round is funding work to turn the face-replacement and de-aging process into a tool that runs inside Nuke rather than a bespoke shot-by-shot service. Details are vendor-supplied and unverified beyond the interview.
stories.why: A Nuke-native face-replacement plugin would change how studios budget de-aging and face work on client jobs.

stories.headline: KeenTools launches KeenFace, photo-to-MetaHuman head generator
stories.body: KeenTools, maker of FaceBuilder, released KeenFace, a browser and API tool that builds production-ready heads in native MetaHuman topology from ordinary reference photos. It outputs 4K PBR maps, automated de-hairing, and a multicam Scan Reconstruction mode. Pricing is pay-as-you-go with free starter credits. Vendor-supplied claims, not independently verified.
stories.why: A direct photo-to-MetaHuman pipeline could replace manual scan cleanup for game and previs character work.

stories.headline: OpenUSD 26.11.1 released
stories.body: Pixar pushed a point release of OpenUSD, version 26.11.1, on GitHub. No changelog detail was included in the feed beyond the version tag. Anyone tracking USD compatibility in a Hydra/Houdini/Karma pipeline should check the release notes directly before upgrading.
stories.why: Any USD point release can affect schema or Hydra compatibility across a studio's whole toolchain.

stories.headline: I Reverse Engineered Mario 64 to Make My Own Game
stories.body: The creator demonstrates 'Reverse Engineer Anything' (REA) to extract exact animation and physics constants (jump heights, gravity, friction) from a legacy console binary to guide AI-driven asset and logic creation in a modern engine.
stories.why: The primary transfer is 'agentic level building.' A TD could use a similar logic where an LLM orchestrates Houdini's Python API to assemble USD stages based on extracted legacy data or natural language prompts.
